findings.explanation: The PR replaces the ownership check `is_owner_or_admin` (previously `user.id == owner_id or user.role == 'admin'` in app/auth.py) with a new implementation in app/ownership.py that returns `user is not None`. This check no longer verifies that the requester owns the object or is an admin — it only confirms a user object exists. Since `g.current_user` is always set by `@require_auth`, the function now returns True for every authenticated user, so any authenticated user can read/update any other user's profile (GET/PUT /users/<id>) and any order by id. This directly violates security-policy.md §2 ('A user may read or update ONLY their own profile... Use is_owner_or_admin(current_user, user_id)') and §3 ('Every endpoint that fetches an order by its identifier MUST verify ownership with is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id)'). The check exists but is incorrect/bypassable.

evidence.content:
if not is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, user_id):
        return jsonify({"error": "forbidden"}), 403

if not is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, user_id):
        return jsonify({"error": "forbidden"}), 403
A user may read or update ONLY their own profile (`/users/<id>`). Administrators may read or update any profile. Use `is_owner_or_admin(current_user, user_id)` for this check.
A user may view ONLY their own orders. Every endpoint that fetches an order by its identifier MUST verify ownership with `is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id)` before returning data.

findings.suggested_fix: Restore the correct ownership logic in app/ownership.py: `return user.id == owner_id or user.role == 'admin'` (and keep the `user is not None` guard if desired). Do not weaken the check to a mere non-None test.
